376	def _task_route_waypoints(origin: Position, task: Task) -> list[Position]:
377	    """Required remaining visit points after *origin* for *task*.
378	
379	    The same pickup/delivery rule is used by first-time assignment, rerouting
380	    after map changes (and the recovery/sidestep planning that shares it) and
381	    checkpoint validation, so the requirement lives in exactly one place:
382	
383	    * Goods not yet collected: the route must still reach the pickup and then
384	      the dropoff. Standing exactly on the pickup makes the pickup leg empty --
385	      the leg contributes no waypoint -- but planning never collects or
386	      completes anything by itself.
387	    * Goods already collected: the robot routes straight to the dropoff, even
388	      when the old pickup cell was closed afterwards; it is never sent back.
389	
390	    When *origin*, pickup and dropoff coincide the list is empty, which
391	    describes a feasible zero-step route and must not be confused with an
392	    unreachable one.
393	    """
394	    waypoints: list[Position] = []
395	    if not task.picked_up and origin != task.pickup:
396	        waypoints.append(task.pickup)
397	    last = waypoints[-1] if waypoints else origin
398	    if task.dropoff != last:
399	        waypoints.append(task.dropoff)
400	    return waypoints

403	def _plan_task_route(
404	    grid: GridMap, origin: Position, task: Task
405	) -> list[Position] | None:
406	    """Shortest feasible route through the task's required waypoints.
407	
408	    The returned list holds the cells after *origin* only, concatenating the
409	    deterministic shortest legs between consecutive required points. It is
410	    ``None`` when any required point cannot be reached, and an empty list for a
411	    feasible route with zero steps (origin already at the only destination).
412	    """
413	    route: list[Position] = []
414	    current = origin
415	    for waypoint in _task_route_waypoints(origin, task):
416	        try:
417	            leg = shortest_path(grid, current, waypoint)
418	        except ValueError:
419	            return None
420	        route.extend(leg)
421	        current = waypoint
422	    return route

425	def _validate_route_walk(
426	    grid: GridMap,
427	    origin: Position,
428	    route: Sequence[object],
429	    *,
430	    robot_id: str,
431	    checkpoint: bool,
432	    blocked_cells: frozenset[Position] | None = None,
433	) -> list[Position]:
434	    """Validate one robot's remaining route as a cell-by-cell map walk.
435	
436	    This is the single place that owns the walking rule shared by direct
437	    fleet construction and checkpoint recovery, so the same legality check is
438	    never edited twice. A route holds the cells still ahead of *origin*:
439	
440	    * every waypoint must parse as two plain integers (booleans are rejected),
441	      and lie inside the map -- a cell in *blocked_cells* is the one kind of
442	      currently obstructed waypoint a version 2 checkpoint recovery may carry
443	      (see below), everything else off the traversable map is rejected;
444	    * the first waypoint must be an up/down/left/right neighbour of *origin*,
445	      so a first waypoint equal to the current cell is rejected;
446	    * every later waypoint must be exactly one orthogonal step from the
447	      previous one -- diagonal moves, multi-cell jumps and two identical
448	      consecutive waypoints are all rejected.
449	
450	    Detours and revisits (including *origin*) are legal, and a route crossing
451	    another robot's cell is never a walk error: traffic is settled while
452	    stepping, not here. The walkability rule deliberately says nothing about
453	    the bound task's pickup/dropoff requirements; checkpoint loading keeps
454	    that separate, stricter business check. The result is a fresh mutable list
455	    of tuple cells, so validating never aliases or mutates the caller's
456	    container and a rejected input leaves every earlier object untouched.
457	
458	    *blocked_cells* is honoured only for checkpoint recovery and names the
459	    cells the recorded map-change history explains: cells open on the base map
460	    that an accepted edit has since closed and that are still closed at save
461	    time. A taskless robot's preset route may legitimately end on such a cell
462	    -- the robot keeps its unconsumed waypoints and simply waits before it --
463	    so those waypoints walk as well as the open cells do. The exemption is
464	    deliberately narrow: only checkpoint loading ever supplies the set (direct
465	    construction leaves it ``None``), only a robot without a bound task may
466	    use it (the caller never passes the set for a task route), and the cells
467	    must be inside the map -- an out-of-bounds waypoint is rejected regardless.
468	    A blocked cell in the base map that no edit explains is never part of the
469	    set, so a route crossing an initial or unexplained obstacle stays illegal.
470	
471	    The two entries keep their existing format and wording differences via
472	    *checkpoint*: direct construction (false) accepts a list or tuple route of
473	    list-or-tuple cells and reports ``route waypoint N`` with a dedicated
474	    message for a first waypoint on the current cell and for repeated
475	    consecutive waypoints; checkpoint loading (true) keeps the strict JSON
476	    list-of-lists format (``_as_pair``), says ``route entry`` and folds both
477	    equal-cell cases into its existing non-adjacency message. The checks
478	    performed are identical either way.
479	    """
480	    allowed_blocked = frozenset() if blocked_cells is None else blocked_cells
481	    waypoints: list[Position] = []
482	    previous = origin
483	    for index, cell in enumerate(route):
484	        if checkpoint:
485	            waypoint = _as_pair(
486	                cell, f"robot {robot_id!r} route entry {index}"
487	            )
488	        else:
489	            waypoint = _as_cell(
490	                cell, f"robot {robot_id!r} route waypoint {index}"
491	            )
492	        if not grid.contains(waypoint) or (
493	            waypoint in grid.obstacles and waypoint not in allowed_blocked
494	        ):
495	            if checkpoint:
496	                raise ValueError(
497	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route entry {list(waypoint)} is "
498	                    "outside the map or inside an obstacle"
499	                )
500	            raise ValueError(
501	                f"robot {robot_id!r} route waypoint {index} "
502	                f"{list(waypoint)} is outside the map or inside an obstacle"
503	            )
504	        if waypoint == previous:
505	            if checkpoint:
506	                # The checkpoint wording treats an equal cell like any other
507	                # non-adjacent step, naming both cells of the offending move.
508	                raise ValueError(
509	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route moves non-adjacently from "
510	                    f"{list(previous)} to {list(waypoint)}"
511	                )
512	            if index == 0:
513	                raise ValueError(
514	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route waypoint 0 {list(waypoint)} "
515	                    "is the robot's current cell; the remaining route must "
516	                    "start with the next cell"
517	                )
518	            raise ValueError(
519	                f"robot {robot_id!r} route repeats cell {list(waypoint)} at "
520	                f"consecutive waypoints {index - 1} and {index}"
521	            )
522	        if (
523	            abs(waypoint[0] - previous[0])
524	            + abs(waypoint[1] - previous[1])
525	            != 1
526	        ):
527	            if checkpoint:
528	                raise ValueError(
529	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route moves non-adjacently from "
530	                    f"{list(previous)} to {list(waypoint)}"
531	                )
532	            if index == 0:
533	                segment = (
534	                    f"from its current position {list(previous)} to route "
535	                    f"waypoint 0 {list(waypoint)}"
536	                )
537	            else:
538	                segment = (
539	                    f"from route waypoint {index - 1} {list(previous)} to "
540	                    f"waypoint {index} {list(waypoint)}"
541	                )
542	            raise ValueError(
543	                f"robot {robot_id!r} route moves non-adjacently {segment}: "
544	                "every step must move one orthogonal cell"
545	            )
546	        waypoints.append(waypoint)
547	        previous = waypoint
548	    return waypoints

552	    def __init__(
553	        self,
554	        grid: GridMap,
555	        robots: list[Robot],
556	        tasks: list[Task],
557	        *,
558	        _routes_prevalidated: bool = False,
559	    ) -> None:
560	        self.grid = grid

562	        # replayed against this baseline.
563	        self.base_grid = grid
564	        # Starting positions share the route coordinates' strict rule: only a
565	        # list or tuple of two plain integers is accepted (booleans, floats and
566	        # strings never act as coordinates), and every accepted position is
567	        # normalized to a fresh integer tuple before any state is committed.
568	        # Task pickup/dropoff points follow the very same rule. This mirrors
569	        # :meth:`_normalize_initial_routes`: all robots and tasks stay exactly
570	        # as the caller passed them until the whole batch -- positions, task
571	        # points, overlaps, ownership and routes -- has passed.
572	        normalized_positions = self._normalize_start_positions(grid, robots)
573	        normalized_task_points = self._normalize_task_coordinates(tasks)
574	        self.robots = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
575	        self.tasks = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
576	        self.tick = 0
577	        self.replay: list[dict[str, object]] = []
578	        self.map_changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
579	        self._map_sequence = 0
580	        self.paused_tasks: set[str] = set()
581	        # Consecutive per-robot waits caused purely by other robots:
582	        # robot_id -> {"blocked_by": [robot_id, ...], "ticks": int}.
583	        self._traffic_waits: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
584	        self._validate_task_ownership(robots, tasks)
585	        if _routes_prevalidated:
586	            # Checkpoint recovery has already run the shared
587	            # :func:`_validate_route_walk` itself -- including its one narrow
588	            # checkpoint exemption for a taskless preset route waiting before
589	            # a history-explained closed cell -- so its already-normalized
590	            # routes must not be re-checked here against the saved grid, where
591	            # those legitimate waypoints look obstructed. Its robots are built
592	            # fresh during loading with validated integer-tuple positions too,
593	            # so nothing needs committing here. Every other constructor check
594	            # above still ran.
595	            return
596	        # Accepted positions, routes and task points share one internal shape
597	        # regardless of how the caller spelled them: an integer tuple for the
598	        # position and each pickup/dropoff, and a mutable list of tuple cells
599	        # for the route. The normalized copies are committed together only
600	        # after every robot and task passed validation, so a rejection -- even
601	        # one buried in a later robot's route or task point -- never touches
602	        # the caller's objects: a fleet whose routes fail is rejected with
603	        # every robot still holding the original position object and route and
604	        # every task still holding its original pickup/dropoff containers. See
605	        # :meth:`_normalize_initial_routes`,
606	        # :meth:`_normalize_start_positions` and
607	        # :meth:`_normalize_task_coordinates`.
608	        normalized_routes = self._normalize_initial_routes(
609	            grid, robots, normalized_positions
610	        )
611	        for robot, position, route in zip(robots, normalized_positions, normalized_routes):
612	            robot.position = position
613	            robot.route = route
614	        for task, (pickup, dropoff) in zip(tasks, normalized_task_points):
615	            task.pickup = pickup
616	            task.dropoff = dropoff

618	    @staticmethod
619	    def _normalize_start_positions(
620	        grid: GridMap, robots: Sequence[Robot]
621	    ) -> list[Position]:
622	        """Validate every robot's starting position and return tuple copies.
623	
624	        The position rule is deliberately the same strict rule the route
625	        waypoints use (:func:`_as_cell`): a position must be a list or tuple
626	        (the two spellings may be mixed across one batch) holding exactly two
627	        plain integers -- booleans are rejected even though they are Python
628	        ints, and floats, strings, missing components, extra components and
629	        non-pair inputs are all refused with :class:`ValueError` naming the
630	        robot and its bad position, never rounded, coerced or padded.
631	
632	        Every accepted position is additionally checked against the map: it
633	        must lie inside the grid and outside every obstacle. Two robots may
634	        not start on the same cell either; the comparison runs on normalized
635	        tuple values, so one robot spelling a cell as ``[x, y]`` and another
636	        as ``(x, y)`` is still a collision, and the error names both robots
637	        involved. Idle robots, task-bound robots and robots carrying preset
638	        routes are all checked -- no robot is skipped to make a batch pass.
639	
640	        The check is read-only: it returns a fresh tuple per robot and commits
641	        nothing itself. The caller assigns the tuples to the robots only once
642	        the whole batch (routes and task bindings included) has passed, so a
643	        later rejection leaves the caller's positions untouched, and the tuple
644	        copy means mutating an originally passed-in list after construction
645	        can never change the created fleet.
646	        """
647	        normalized: list[Position] = []
648	        occupied: dict[Position, str] = {}
649	        for robot in robots:
650	            position = _as_cell(
651	                robot.position, f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} starting position"
652	            )
653	            if not grid.traversable(position):
654	                raise ValueError(
655	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} starting position {list(position)} "
656	                    "is outside the map or inside an obstacle"
657	                )
658	            other_id = occupied.get(position)
659	            if other_id is not None:
660	                raise ValueError(
661	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} starting position {list(position)} "
662	                    f"is already occupied by robot {other_id!r}: robots cannot "
663	                    "share an initial cell"
664	                )
665	            occupied[position] = robot.robot_id
666	            normalized.append(position)
667	        return normalized

669	    @staticmethod
670	    def _normalize_task_coordinates(
671	        tasks: Sequence[Task],
672	    ) -> list[tuple[Position, Position]]:
673	        """Validate every task's pickup and dropoff and return tuple copies.
674	
675	        Task points share the strict position rule (:func:`_as_cell`): each one
676	        must be a list or tuple (the two spellings may be mixed within one
677	        task and across one batch) holding exactly two plain integers --
678	        booleans are rejected even though they are Python ints, and floats
679	        (even ``1.0``), strings, nulls, missing components, extra components
680	        and non-pair inputs are all refused with :class:`ValueError` naming the
681	        task and whether its pickup or its dropoff is at fault, never rounded,
682	        padded or coerced. This runs for every task regardless of state --
683	        waiting for assignment, en route to pickup, already carrying the goods
684	        or already completed -- so a malformed point in a finished historical
685	        record is refused at construction just like one in a pending task.
686	
687	        Coordinate validity is deliberately kept separate from reachability:
688	        whether a robot can currently reach the points is never judged here, so
689	        a well-formed task whose pickup is currently unreachable keeps waiting
690	        exactly as before, and a loaded task whose pickup cell has since been
691	        closed keeps the goods and its binding -- neither is an error.
692	
693	        The check is read-only: it returns a fresh integer tuple per point and
694	        commits nothing itself. The caller assigns the tuples to the tasks only
695	        once the whole batch (positions, ownership and routes included) has
696	        passed, so a later rejection leaves the caller's tasks holding their
697	        original pickup/dropoff containers, and the tuple copy means mutating
698	        an originally passed-in list after construction can never change the
699	        created fleet. A list and a tuple naming one cell normalize to equal
700	        tuples, so they can never make a robot miss a pickup or fail a delivery
701	        merely because of the container type.
702	        """
703	        normalized: list[tuple[Position, Position]] = []
704	        for task in tasks:
705	            pickup = _as_cell(task.pickup, f"task {task.task_id!r} pickup")
706	            dropoff = _as_cell(task.dropoff, f"task {task.task_id!r} dropoff")
707	            normalized.append((pickup, dropoff))
708	        return normalized

710	    @staticmethod
711	    def _validate_task_ownership(robots: Sequence[Robot], tasks: Sequence[Task]) -> None:
712	        """Reject impossible initial bindings between robots and tasks.
713	
714	        The very same ownership requirements back direct construction and
715	        checkpoint loading, so they live in exactly one place. The mutual
716	        binding only governs work still in progress:
717	
718	        * A robot that declares a task must name a task that exists, is not
719	          completed yet, and is assigned back to that same robot.
720	        * An unfinished task that names an owner must name an existing robot
721	          whose current task it is; an unfinished task with the goods already
722	          collected additionally must have an owner.
723	        * A robot can therefore never be claimed by two unfinished tasks: the
724	          second task's owner points at a robot that executes another task.
725	        * A completed task must carry the picked-up mark *and* a historical
726	          owner (a non-null ``assigned_robot``); see below.
727	
728	        Completed tasks are history, not work in progress, but the history must
729	        still be coherent: a finished task must carry both the picked-up mark
730	        and the id of the robot that finished it -- ``None`` means "no record",
731	        never an anonymous completion, even when the pickup point and the
732	        dropoff coincide. Neither gap is repaired (the owner is not filled in,
733	        the pickup mark is not flipped, nothing is reassigned or dropped); the
734	        fleet is rejected as a whole with a :class:`ValueError` naming the task
735	        and the exact contradiction. The historical owner itself is bound by
736	        none of the in-progress rules: it need not be idle or name the task
737	        back, may already work a new task, may have finished several tasks, and
738	        may even be absent from the fleet, so historical records never occupy a
739	        robot or take part in new task assignment. Unassigned, not-yet-collected
740	        tasks simply wait -- even when no robot can reach them -- and are not an
741	        ownership error. Nothing here rewrites a binding or drops a task; an
742	        inconsistent input is rejected as a whole, leaving the caller's objects
743	        untouched.
744	        """
745	        robot_by_id = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
746	        task_by_id = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
747	        for robot in robots:
748	            if robot.task_id is None:
749	                continue
750	            task = task_by_id.get(robot.task_id)
751	            if task is None:
752	                raise ValueError(
753	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes unknown task "
754	                    f"{robot.task_id!r}"
755	                )
756	            if task.completed:
757	                raise ValueError(
758	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} "
759	                    "that is already completed"
760	                )
761	            if task.assigned_robot != robot.robot_id:
762	                raise ValueError(
763	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} "
764	                    f"but the task is assigned to {task.assigned_robot!r}"
765	                )
766	        for task in tasks:
767	            if task.completed:
768	                # A finished task is a fixed historical record: the goods must
769	                # have been collected and a historical finishing robot must be
770	                # named. The very same requirement backs direct construction
771	                # and checkpoint recovery, so a document that could never be
772	                # loaded again can never be built in the first place. This is
773	                # judged purely from the record -- even a task whose pickup
774	                # point equals its dropoff is not presumed collected -- and the
775	                # recorded robot is history only: it is never looked up, so it
776	                # may be retired, idle or already busy with another task, and
777	                # several completed tasks may name the same robot without ever
778	                # counting as occupying it.
779	                if not task.picked_up:
780	                    if task.assigned_robot is None:
781	                        raise ValueError(
782	                            f"task {task.task_id!r} is marked completed but was "
783	                            "never picked up and has no historical assigned robot"
784	                        )
785	                    raise ValueError(
786	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} is marked completed but never "
787	                        "picked up, even though historical robot "
788	                        f"{task.assigned_robot!r} is recorded for it"
789	                    )
790	                if task.assigned_robot is None:
791	                    raise ValueError(
792	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} is marked completed and picked up "
793	                        "but has no historical assigned robot"
794	                    )
795	                continue
796	            if task.picked_up and task.assigned_robot is None:
797	                raise ValueError(
798	                    f"task {task.task_id!r} is picked up but has no assigned robot"
799	                )
800	            if task.assigned_robot is not None:
801	                owner = robot_by_id.get(task.assigned_robot)
802	                if owner is None:
803	                    raise ValueError(
804	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} is assigned to unknown robot "
805	                        f"{task.assigned_robot!r}"
806	                    )
807	                if owner.task_id != task.task_id:
808	                    raise ValueError(
809	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} claims robot {owner.robot_id!r} "
810	                        f"but the robot executes {owner.task_id!r}"
811	                    )

813	    @staticmethod
814	    def _normalize_initial_routes(
815	        grid: GridMap,
816	        robots: Sequence[Robot],
817	        positions: Sequence[Position],
818	    ) -> list[list[Position]]:
819	        """Validate every remaining route and return normalized copies.
820	
821	        Every robot is checked, idle or task-bound, via the single shared walk
822	        validator :func:`_validate_route_walk` -- the same coordinate shape,
823	        map-walkability and one-orthogonal-step rule checkpoint recovery uses
824	        -- so a walking rule never has to be changed in two places. The outer
825	        route may be a list or tuple and each waypoint may itself be a list or
826	        tuple of two plain integers -- booleans are not integers here, and
827	        wrong lengths or element types raise :class:`ValueError` instead of
828	        leaking unpacking or hashing failures. The forms may be mixed freely;
829	        only the coordinate order matters, not the container types.
830	
831	        *positions* holds the already-normalized tuple starting positions from
832	        :meth:`_normalize_start_positions`, paired one-to-one with *robots*:
833	        every route is walked from the tuple form so a first waypoint equal to
834	        the start cell is recognized regardless of how the caller spelled
835	        either container.
836	
837	        Accepted routes are returned as mutable lists of tuple cells, the one
838	        shape the rest of the engine relies on (head consumption with
839	        ``pop(0)`` and hashable cells for road and occupancy checks). Empty
840	        lists and tuples both normalize to an empty route. Routes need not be
841	        shortest paths and may revisit cells, and traffic (a route crossing
842	        another robot's cell, or routes sharing a cell) is left to execution:
843	        only walkability on the given map is judged.
844	
845	        The check is read-only -- :func:`_validate_route_walk` builds fresh
846	        lists, and the caller commits them itself only once every robot has
847	        passed, so a rejected fleet is rejected as a whole: an error on a
848	        later robot or at the end of a route never truncates, pads, reorders
849	        or otherwise modifies an earlier robot or any caller object. The
850	        shared walk check says nothing about tasks; direct construction keeps
851	        accepting any walkable route, while checkpoint loading keeps its own
852	        stricter validation that also covers the pickup/dropoff rules.
853	        """
854	        normalized: list[list[Position]] = []
855	        for robot, position in zip(robots, positions):
856	            route = robot.route
857	            if not isinstance(route, (list, tuple)):
858	                raise ValueError(
859	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} remaining route must be a list "
860	                    "of [x, y] waypoints"
861	                )
862	            normalized.append(
863	                _validate_route_walk(
864	                    grid,
865	                    position,
866	                    route,
867	                    robot_id=robot.robot_id,
868	                    checkpoint=False,
869	                )
870	            )
871	        return normalized

877	    def modify_obstacles(
878	        self,
879	        added: Sequence[Position] = (),
880	        removed: Sequence[Position] = (),
881	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
882	        """Close and/or reopen cells without advancing the simulation.
883	
884	        The whole request is validated before anything changes: coordinates
885	        must be two plain integers (booleans are rejected), lie inside the
886	        map, no cell may appear in both lists, and newly added obstacles may
887	        not cover a robot's current cell. Duplicate coordinates inside one
888	        batch are processed once. Adding an existing obstacle or removing a
889	        traversable cell is a no-op. Invalid requests raise :class:`ValueError`
890	        and leave every part of the state untouched.
891	
892	        Assigned unfinished tasks keep their robot: routes are replanned
893	        against the new map, or, when a required point is unreachable, cleared
894	        while the task is suspended. No tick is recorded, no robot moves and no
895	        distance is accumulated.
896	        """
897	        add_cells = self._normalize_cells(added, "added")
898	        remove_cells = self._normalize_cells(removed, "removed")
899	        conflict = set(add_cells) & set(remove_cells)
900	        if conflict:
901	            cell = sorted(conflict)[0]
902	            raise ValueError(
903	                f"cell {list(cell)} is both added and removed in the same request"
904	            )
905	        occupied = {robot.position for robot in self.robots.values()}
906	        for cell in add_cells:
907	            if cell in occupied:
908	                raise ValueError(
909	                    f"cannot add obstacle at {list(cell)}: a robot currently occupies it"
910	                )
911	        return self._apply_map_change(add_cells, remove_cells)
912	
913	    def _normalize_cells(self, cells: Sequence[Position], label: str) -> list[Position]:
914	        if isinstance(cells, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(cells, (list, tuple)):
915	            raise ValueError(f"{label} cells must be provided as a list of [x, y] pairs")
916	        seen: set[Position] = set()
917	        ordered: list[Position] = []
918	        for index, cell in enumerate(cells):
919	            position = _as_cell(cell, f"{label} cell {index}")
920	            if not self.grid.contains(position):
921	                raise ValueError(f"{label} cell {list(position)} lies outside the map")
922	            if position in seen:
923	                # Batch-internal duplicates are handled once, not rejected.
924	                continue
925	            seen.add(position)
926	            ordered.append(position)
927	        return ordered

929	    def _apply_map_change(
930	        self, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
931	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
932	        obstacles = set(self.grid.obstacles)
933	        actual_added = [cell for cell in added if cell not in obstacles]
934	        obstacles.update(actual_added)
935	        actual_removed = [cell for cell in removed if cell in obstacles]
936	        obstacles.difference_update(actual_removed)
937	        if not actual_added and not actual_removed:
938	            return self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, [], [])
939	
940	        # Everything below only runs once the batch was fully validated and is
941	        # known to change the map.
942	        self.grid = GridMap(self.grid.width, self.grid.height, frozenset(obstacles))
943	        self._map_sequence += 1
944	        record = self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, actual_added, actual_removed)
945	        self.map_changes.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
946	        self.replay.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
947	        self._reroute_after_map_change()
948	        self._reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change()
949	        return copy.deepcopy(record)

951	    def _map_change_record(
952	        self, sequence: int, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
953	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
954	        return {
955	            "type": "map_change",
956	            "tick": self.tick,
957	            "sequence": sequence,
958	            "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
959	            "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
960	        }

962	    def _plan_route(
963	        self, robot: Robot, task: Task, start: Position | None = None
964	    ) -> list[Position] | None:
965	        """Shortest current->pickup->dropoff route, or None if unreachable.
966	
967	        *start* overrides the robot's current position, which is how sidestep
968	        candidates are evaluated without moving the robot first. The
969	        pickup/delivery rule itself is shared with first-time assignment and
970	        checkpoint validation via :func:`_plan_task_route`.
971	        """
972	        origin = robot.position if start is None else start
973	        return _plan_task_route(self.grid, origin, task)

975	    def _reroute_after_map_change(self) -> None:
976	        for task in self.tasks.values():
977	            if task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
978	                continue
979	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
980	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
981	                continue
982	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
983	            if route is None:
984	                robot.route = []
985	                self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
986	            else:
987	                # Only the route is refreshed here; pickup/delivery are
988	                # confirmed at step start (or were already recorded).
989	                robot.route = route
990	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)
991	
992	    def _recover_paused_tasks(self) -> None:
993	        """Resume tasks suspended by map unreachability where possible."""
994	        for task_id in sorted(self.paused_tasks):
995	            task = self.tasks.get(task_id)
996	            if task is None or task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
997	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
998	                continue
999	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
1000	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
1001	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
1002	                continue
1003	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
1004	            if route is None:
1005	                robot.route = []
1006	                continue
1007	            robot.route = route
1008	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
1009	            self._finish_if_arrived(robot)

1015	    def _route_cells(self, exclude_id: str) -> set[Position]:
1016	        """Cells every robot except *exclude_id* still plans to drive through."""
1017	        cells: set[Position] = set()
1018	        for robot in self.robots.values():
1019	            if robot.robot_id != exclude_id:
1020	                cells.update(robot.route)
1021	        return cells

1023	    def _safe_side_cells(
1024	        self,
1025	        robot: Robot,
1026	        occupied: Mapping[Position, str],
1027	        reserved: Mapping[Position, str],
1028	        forbidden: Iterable[Position] = (),
1029	    ) -> Iterator[Position]:
1030	        """Adjacent cells *robot* may actually side-step onto this tick.
1031	
1032	        The very same safety rule backs every side-step decision -- an idle
1033	        robot yielding for someone, a busy robot dodging a blocker itself, and
1034	        the hypothetical leave checks behind a retreat -- so the shared
1035	        conditions live exactly here. A cell qualifies only when it:
1036	
1037	        * lies inside the map with no obstacle (``GridMap.neighbors`` already
1038	          skips anything else),
1039	        * is held by no robot in the given (possibly hypothetical) layout,
1040	        * was not reserved by a move that already happened this tick,
1041	        * lies on no other robot's remaining route (the moving robot's own
1042	          route is excluded), and
1043	        * is not among *forbidden*: cells that are physically free but unsafe
1044	          for the caller's scenario, such as the requester's own cell (a
1045	          side-step there would swap the two robots within one tick) or the
1046	          retreating requester's replanned path (parking there only moves the
1047	          blockage onto a cell the requester must re-enter).
1048	
1049	        Neighbours are yielded in the deterministic ``GridMap.neighbors``
1050	        order (up, left, right, down); callers keep their own selection rules.
1051	        """
1052	        blocked = set(forbidden)
1053	        blocked.update(self._route_cells(exclude_id=robot.robot_id))
1054	        for cell in self.grid.neighbors(robot.position):
1055	            if cell in blocked or cell in occupied or cell in reserved:
1056	                continue
1057	            yield cell

1059	    def _idle_sidestep_cell(
1060	        self,
1061	        blocker: Robot,
1062	        requester: Robot,
1063	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
1064	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
1065	    ) -> Position | None:
1066	        """Free side-cell a parked blocker can yield to, or None.
1067	
1068	        Only a robot with no bound task and no remaining route is parked and
1069	        asked to yield; callers must never route a taskless-but-moving robot
1070	        here. The requester's own cell is forbidden (yielding onto it would
1071	        swap the two robots within one tick); every other safety condition is
1072	        shared via :meth:`_safe_side_cells`, so the blocker never trades one
1073	        blockage for another. The first candidate in neighbour order wins.
1074	        """
1075	        return next(
1076	            self._safe_side_cells(
1077	                blocker, occupied, reserved, forbidden=(requester.position,)
1078	            ),
1079	            None,
1080	        )

1082	    def _self_sidestep(
1083	        self,
1084	        robot: Robot,
1085	        task: Task | None,
1086	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
1087	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
1088	        already_moved: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
1089	    ) -> tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None:
1090	        """Best side cell plus replanned route for a blocked robot, or None.
1091	
1092	        Only cells off every other robot's planned route qualify, and only if
1093	        the task remains reachable from there. A candidate that merely retreats
1094	        along the corridor only to face the very same blocker again on the next
1095	        tick is rejected too: such a move records mileage and gets undone
1096	        forever instead of making progress, even when more empty cells stretch
1097	        out behind the robot. Candidates are ranked by replanned route length
1098	        with the deterministic neighbor order (up, left, right, down) breaking
1099	        ties. *already_moved* names robots that have used their one move of
1100	        this tick and therefore cannot vacate a cell to resolve the block.
1101	        """
1102	        if task is None or task.completed:
1103	            return None
1104	        destination = robot.route[0]
1105	        blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
1106	        if blocker_id is None:
1107	            blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
1108	        best: tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None = None
1109	        best_length = 0
1110	        # Candidates arrive in neighbour order (up, left, right, down), so the
1111	        # first candidate of the minimum replanned length automatically keeps
1112	        # that order as the tie break.
1113	        for cell in self._safe_side_cells(robot, occupied, reserved):
1114	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task, start=cell)
1115	            if route is None:
1116	                continue
1117	            if (
1118	                blocker_id is not None
1119	                and blocker_id != robot.robot_id
1120	                and self._is_bounceback_retreat(
1121	                    robot, cell, route, blocker_id, occupied, reserved, already_moved
1122	                )
1123	            ):
1124	                # The replanned route immediately returns through the cell the
1125	                # robot is vacating and the blocker cannot use that opening to
1126	                # leave: the move would be undone on the next tick.
1127	                continue
1128	            if best is None or len(route) < best_length:
1129	                best = (cell, route)
1130	                best_length = len(route)
1131	        return best

1133	    def _is_bounceback_retreat(
1134	        self,
1135	        robot: Robot,
1136	        side: Position,
1137	        replanned: Sequence[Position],
1138	        blocker_id: str,
1139	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
1140	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
1141	        already_moved: frozenset[str],
1142	    ) -> bool:
1143	        """Whether stepping to *side* only sends the robot back to the block.
1144	
1145	        A retreat is futile when the replanned route leads straight back through
1146	        the robot's current cell and still runs through the blocker's cell (so
1147	        the side move is undone next tick with the same blocker ahead) while
1148	        the blocker cannot leave its own cell through the gap that opens up.
1149	        A route that bypasses the blocker entirely is a genuine detour and is
1150	        never rejected here.
1151	        """
1152	        if not replanned or replanned[0] != robot.position:
1153	            return False
1154	        blocker = self.robots.get(blocker_id)
1155	        if blocker is None or blocker.position not in replanned:
1156	            return False
1157	        # Hypothetical end-of-tick layout: the requester has vacated its cell
1158	        # and stands on the candidate side cell.
1159	        hyp_occupied = dict(occupied)
1160	        del hyp_occupied[robot.position]
1161	        hyp_occupied[side] = robot.robot_id
1162	        # The requester only gets back onto its route by driving through these
1163	        # cells, so a blocker may only "leave" by driving on, never by parking
1164	        # on the replanned route. The requester cannot make a second move
1165	        # within this tick, and neither can a robot that already moved.
1166	        blocked_path = frozenset(replanned)
1167	        return not self._can_vacate(
1168	            blocker,
1169	            robot,
1170	            hyp_occupied,
1171	            reserved,
1172	            frozenset({robot.robot_id}) | already_moved,
1173	            blocked_path,
1174	        )

1176	    def _side_exit_cells(
1177	        self,
1178	        robot: Robot,
1179	        task: Task,
1180	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
1181	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
1182	        blocked_path: frozenset[Position],
1183	    ) -> Iterator[tuple[Position, list[Position]]]:
1184	        """Side cells a busy robot could escape to, with their replanned routes.
1185	
1186	        Only cells off every other robot's planned route that keep the robot's
1187	        task reachable are offered, in deterministic neighbour order. Whether
1188	        such a cell is a genuine way out -- or just moves the robot aside for
1189	        one tick before it is driven back onto the same blocked corridor -- is
1190	        judged by the caller as it scans the candidates.
1191	        """
1192	        for side_cell in self._safe_side_cells(
1193	            robot, occupied, reserved, forbidden=blocked_path
1194	        ):
1195	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task, start=side_cell)
1196	            if route is not None:
1197	                yield side_cell, route

1199	    def _can_vacate(
1200	        self,
1201	        blocker: Robot,
1202	        requester: Robot,
1203	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
1204	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
1205	        checking: frozenset[str],
1206	        blocked_path: frozenset[Position],
1207	    ) -> bool:
1208	        """Whether *blocker* can leave its cell this tick in the given layout.
1209	
1210	        A parked blocker (no task and no remaining route) leaves only by
1211	        yielding onto a safe side cell for the requesting robot; a moving
1212	        blocker -- task-bound, or taskless but still driving a remaining route
1213	        -- leaves by driving onto its next waypoint (possibly following a
1214	        chain of robots that all move this tick); a task-bound one may also
1215	        sidestep onto a free adjacent cell itself. Robots paused by map
1216	        unreachability never move. *checking* names robots already on the
1217	        dependency chain (including robots that used their one move of this
1218	        tick), so meeting one again closes a cyclic dependency -- a head-on
1219	        deadlock, or the requester itself -- and never proves an exit merely
1220	        because every robot on the cycle still carries a route.
1221	        *blocked_path* holds the cells the retreating requester must drive
1222	        back through: another robot parking there only moves the blockage, so
1223	        such sidesteps do not count as leaving (driving on along the cell on
1224	        the blocker's own route does).
1225	
1226	        A task-bound blocker's own side step is judged by the same standard as
1227	        the requester's retreat: it counts as leaving only when the replanned
1228	        route from the side cell does not lead straight back through the cell
1229	        being vacated into another robot that cannot get out of the way
1230	        either. A side cell the blocker must leave again on the next tick to
1231	        re-face the very same unyielding jam further down the corridor is no
1232	        way out, so it never justifies the retreat behind it.
1233	
1234	        The follow chain can run through an arbitrarily long legal queue, so
1235	        the search is an explicit stack rather than Python recursion: a queue
1236	        of twelve hundred robots ending at a parked robot with no side cell
1237	        must report "cannot vacate" from a normal ``step()`` instead of
1238	        raising :class:`RecursionError`. Each frame is
1239	        ``(robot, occupied, checking, blocked_path, resume)``: a nested
1240	        hypothetical (the blocker having stepped aside) works with its own
1241	        layout and no-go cells, so both travel with the frame. *resume* is
1242	        ``None`` on a frame's first visit and afterwards holds the robot's
1243	        not-yet-tried side-exit candidates as a stateful iterator. A frame
1244	        examined for the first time first tries the free-waypoint and
1245	        follow-chain rules; only when the chain ahead comes back empty does it
1246	        resume at its own side-cell scan, continuing exactly where that scan

1251	            tuple[
1252	                Robot,
1253	                dict[Position, str],
1254	                frozenset[str],
1255	                frozenset[Position],
1256	                Iterator[tuple[Position, list[Position]]] | None,
1257	            ]
1258	        ] = [frame]
1259	        while stack:

1261	            if current.robot_id in cur_checking:
1262	                # The chain has folded back onto a robot it already depends
1263	                # on: a cycle cannot vacate itself. The frame that followed
1264	                # this one simply resumes with its own side-cell options.
1265	                continue
1266	            task = self.tasks[current.task_id] if current.task_id is not None else None
1267	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
1268	                continue
1269	            if not current.route:
1270	                if task is not None:
1271	                    # A busy robot with no route left only arrives/finishes this
1272	                    # tick; it never drives or sidesteps for anyone.
1273	                    continue

1275	                # yielding onto a safe side cell for the requesting robot; it does
1276	                # so onto the first safe cell in neighbour order. When that
1277	                # particular cell sits on the path the retreating requester must
1278	                # re-enter, parking there only relocates the blockage instead of
1279	                # clearing it, so it does not count as leaving.
1280	                side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(current, requester, cur_occupied, reserved)
1281	                if side is not None and side not in cur_blocked_path:
1282	                    return True
1283	                continue
1284	            if resume is None:
1285	                ahead = current.route[0]
1286	                if (
1287	                    self.grid.traversable(ahead)
1288	                    and ahead not in cur_occupied
1289	                    and ahead not in reserved
1290	                ):
1291	                    return True
1292	                occupant_id = cur_occupied.get(ahead) or reserved.get(ahead)
1293	                if (
1294	                    occupant_id is not None
1295	                    and occupant_id != current.robot_id
1296	                    and occupant_id not in cur_checking
1297	                ):
1298	                    # The robot could follow the occupant once that robot
1299	                    # vacates its cell this same tick. This frame resumes with
1300	                    # its side-cell scan only after the chain ahead proves it
1301	                    # cannot clear, mirroring the recursive call order.
1302	                    stack.append(
1303	                        (
1304	                            current,
1305	                            cur_occupied,
1306	                            cur_checking,
1307	                            cur_blocked_path,
1308	                            self._side_exit_cells(
1309	                                current, task, cur_occupied, reserved, cur_blocked_path
1310	                            )
1311	                            if task is not None
1312	                            else iter(()),
1313	                        )
1314	                    )
1315	                    stack.append(
1316	                        (
1317	                            self.robots[occupant_id],
1318	                            cur_occupied,
1319	                            cur_checking | {current.robot_id},
1320	                            cur_blocked_path,
1321	                            None,
1322	                        )
1323	                    )
1324	                    continue
1325	                resume = (
1326	                    self._side_exit_cells(
1327	                        current, task, cur_occupied, reserved, cur_blocked_path
1328	                    )
1329	                    if task is not None
1330	                    else iter(())
1331	                )
1332	            if task is None:
1333	                # A taskless robot that still drives a remaining route never
1334	                # sidesteps off it -- not even to unblock a requester -- so a side
1335	                # cell cannot count as a way out for it.
1336	                continue
1337	            # Otherwise the task-bound blocker might sidestep onto a free side
1338	            # cell itself, but not onto a cell the retreating requester still has
1339	            # to use -- parking there only moves the blockage.
1340	            chained = False
1341	            for side_cell, route in resume:
1342	                if not route or route[0] != current.position:
1343	                    # A genuine exit: the robot drives on elsewhere instead of
1344	                    # returning onto the cell it just vacated.
1345	                    return True
1346	                # The replanned route leads straight back through the cell
1347	                # being vacated. That still counts as leaving when the way
1348	                # back is clear, or when whoever holds it can clear out in
1349	                # turn -- but not when the robot would re-face a jam that has
1350	                # no exit of its own, because then the side step is undone on
1351	                # the next tick with nothing gained.
1352	                hyp_occupied = dict(cur_occupied)
1353	                del hyp_occupied[current.position]
