1768	    @classmethod
1769	    def _from_checkpoint(cls, data: object) -> FleetSimulator:
1770	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
1771	            raise ValueError("checkpoint root must be a JSON object")
1772	
1773	        version = data.get("version")
1774	        if not _is_int(version):
1775	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'version' must be an integer")
1776	        if version not in _SUPPORTED_VERSIONS:
1777	            raise ValueError(
1778	                f"unsupported checkpoint version {version}; supported versions: "
1779	                f"{sorted(_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS)}"
1780	            )
1781	
1782	        grid = cls._load_grid(data)
1783	        tick = cls._load_tick(data)
1784	        robot_records, task_records = cls._load_entities(data)
1785	
1786	        map_changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
1787	        paused: set[str] = set()
1788	        if version == 1:
1789	            replay = cls._load_legacy_replay(data)
1790	            base_grid = grid
1791	            # Version 1 has no change history: every blocked waypoint keeps
1792	            # being judged purely against the saved grid, exactly as before.
1793	            history_closed: frozenset[Position] = frozenset()
1794	        else:
1795	            replay = cls._load_replay(data)
1796	            map_changes = cls._load_map_changes(data)
1797	            paused = cls._load_paused_tasks(data)
1798	            base_grid = cls._load_base_grid(data)
1799	            if (base_grid.width, base_grid.height) != (grid.width, grid.height):
1800	                raise ValueError("base grid dimensions must match the current grid")
1801	            cls._validate_map_history(base_grid, grid, map_changes)
1802	            history_closed = cls._history_closed_cells(base_grid, map_changes)
1803	
1804	        robots: list[Robot] = []
1805	        for record in robot_records:
1806	            position = _as_pair(record["position"], f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} position")
1807	            if not grid.traversable(position):
1808	                raise ValueError(
1809	                    f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} position {list(position)} is outside "
1810	                    "the map or inside an obstacle"
1811	                )
1812	            # Walkability uses the very same shared cell-by-cell rule as
1813	            # direct construction (strict JSON list format and checkpoint
1814	            # wording preserved); the task pickup/dropoff rules are a separate
1815	            # check below. The only relaxation checkpoint recovery adds over
1816	            # direct construction is for a robot with no bound task whose
1817	            # preset route waits before a cell the recorded edits closed: such
1818	            # a waypoint is unobstructed on the base map and still blocked on
1819	            # the saved one, so the route keeps it instead of being rejected
1820	            # as an illegal walk. A bound task route, an initial obstacle and
1821	            # anything the history cannot explain stay strict.
1822	            allowed_blocked = (
1823	                history_closed
1824	                if record["task_id"] is None
1825	                else frozenset()
1826	            )
1827	            route: list[tuple[int, int]] = _validate_route_walk(
1828	                grid,
1829	                position,
1830	                record["route"],
1831	                robot_id=record["robot_id"],
1832	                checkpoint=True,
1833	                blocked_cells=allowed_blocked,
1834	            )
1835	            distance = record["distance_travelled"]
1836	            if not _is_int(distance) or distance < 0:
1837	                raise ValueError(
1838	                    f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} distance_travelled must be a "
1839	                    "non-negative integer"
1840	                )
1841	            robots.append(Robot(record["robot_id"], position, route, record["task_id"], distance))
1842	
1843	        tasks: list[Task] = []
1844	        for record in task_records:
1845	            pickup = _as_pair(record["pickup"], f"task {record['task_id']!r} pickup")
1846	            dropoff = _as_pair(record["dropoff"], f"task {record['task_id']!r} dropoff")
1847	            tasks.append(
1848	                Task(
1849	                    record["task_id"],
1850	                    pickup,
1851	                    dropoff,
1852	                    record["assigned_robot"],
1853	                    record["picked_up"],
1854	                    record["completed"],
1855	                )
1856	            )
1857	
1858	        robot_by_id = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
1859	        task_by_id = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
1860	
1861	        # Ownership and the completed-task history are judged with the exact
1862	        # rules direct construction uses -- mutual bindings for work in
1863	        # progress, a collected task that may never lack its carrier, and a
1864	        # finished task that must keep its picked-up mark and historical owner
1865	        # -- so a checkpoint can never load a completion that direct
1866	        # construction would have rejected (or vice versa).
1867	        cls._validate_task_ownership(robots, tasks)
1868	
1869	        cls._validate_paused_state(paused, task_by_id, robot_by_id, grid)
1870	        cls._validate_active_task_routes(paused, task_by_id, robot_by_id)
1871	        traffic_waits = cls._load_traffic_waits(data, robot_by_id)
1872	
1873	        replay_change_frames = cls._replay_map_change_frames(replay)
1874	        if replay_change_frames != map_changes:
1875	            raise ValueError("replay map-change frames do not match 'map_changes' history")
1876	
1877	        simulator = cls(grid, robots, tasks, _routes_prevalidated=True)
1878	        simulator.base_grid = base_grid
1879	        simulator.tick = tick
1880	        simulator.replay = copy.deepcopy(replay)
1881	        simulator.map_changes = copy.deepcopy(map_changes)
1882	        simulator._map_sequence = len(map_changes)
1883	        simulator.paused_tasks = set(paused)
1884	        simulator._traffic_waits = traffic_waits
1885	        # Version 1 has no edit history: its saved grid is the baseline and
1886	        # applies to every tick frame. Version 2 replays the recorded changes
1887	        # alongside the frames so each frame is judged against its contemporary
1888	        # map.
1889	        cls._validate_replay_positions(replay, tick, robot_by_id, base_grid, map_changes)
1890	        cls._validate_replay_completion(replay, tick, task_by_id)
1891	        return simulator

1911	    @classmethod
1912	    def _load_map_definition(
1913	        cls,
1914	        data: Mapping[str, object],
1915	        field_name: str,
1916	        *,
1917	        map_label: str,
1918	        obstacle_label: str,
1919	    ) -> GridMap:
1920	        """Validate one checkpoint map definition and build its grid.
1921	
1922	        This is the single place that owns the map-definition rule shared by
1923	        the current ``grid`` and the version 2 ``base_grid``, so a format or
1924	        value rule never has to be changed in two places: the field must be an
1925	        object with positive integer ``width``/``height`` (booleans are not
1926	        integers) and an ``obstacles`` list of ``[x, y]`` integer pairs, each
1927	        lying inside its own map. An empty obstacle list is legal, and a
1928	        coordinate repeated within the list denotes a single obstacle. Nothing
1929	        is coerced -- strings, floats and booleans are rejected, never
1930	        converted -- and the file-format judgement is not relaxed just because
1931	        a grid could be built from the values.
1932	
1933	        The two definitions are validated independently and keep their own
1934	        contents: neither map is ever copied from the other. Only the wording
1935	        differs between the two entry points, via *map_label* (``grid`` /
1936	        ``base grid``) and *obstacle_label* (``obstacle`` / ``base obstacle``),
1937	        so an error still names the map and the exact dimension or obstacle
1938	        entry at fault. Cross-definition rules -- matching dimensions and a
1939	        history that replays the base grid onto the current one -- are checked
1940	        separately afterwards and stay distinct rejection reasons.
1941	        """
1942	        raw = cls._require_field(data, field_name)
1943	        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
1944	            raise ValueError(f"checkpoint field {field_name!r} must be an object")
1945	        width = raw.get("width")
1946	        height = raw.get("height")
1947	        if not _is_int(width) or width <= 0:
1948	            raise ValueError(
1949	                f"checkpoint {map_label} width must be a positive integer"
1950	            )
1951	        if not _is_int(height) or height <= 0:
1952	            raise ValueError(
1953	                f"checkpoint {map_label} height must be a positive integer"
1954	            )
1955	        raw_obstacles = raw.get("obstacles")
1956	        if not isinstance(raw_obstacles, list):
1957	            raise ValueError(f"checkpoint {map_label} 'obstacles' must be a list")
1958	        obstacles: set[tuple[int, int]] = set()
1959	        for index, cell in enumerate(raw_obstacles):
1960	            obstacle = _as_pair(cell, f"{obstacle_label} entry {index}")
1961	            if not (0 <= obstacle[0] < width and 0 <= obstacle[1] < height):
1962	                raise ValueError(
1963	                    f"{obstacle_label} {list(obstacle)} lies outside the map"
1964	                )
1965	            obstacles.add(obstacle)
1966	        try:
1967	            return GridMap(width, height, frozenset(obstacles))
1968	        except ValueError as exc:
1969	            raise ValueError(f"invalid checkpoint {map_label}: {exc}") from exc

1978	    @classmethod
1979	    def _load_entities(
1980	        cls, data: Mapping[str, object]
1981	    ) -> tuple[list[dict[str, object]], list[dict[str, object]]]:
1982	        raw_robots = cls._require_field(data, "robots")
1983	        raw_tasks = cls._require_field(data, "tasks")
1984	        if not isinstance(raw_robots, list):
1985	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'robots' must be a list")
1986	        if not isinstance(raw_tasks, list):
1987	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'tasks' must be a list")
1988	
1989	        robot_records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
1990	        robot_ids: set[str] = set()
1991	        for index, record in enumerate(raw_robots):
1992	            if not isinstance(record, dict):
1993	                raise ValueError(f"robot entry {index} must be an object")
1994	            robot_id = record.get("robot_id")
1995	            if not isinstance(robot_id, str):
1996	                raise ValueError(f"robot entry {index} field 'robot_id' must be a string")
1997	            if robot_id in robot_ids:
1998	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate robot id {robot_id!r} in checkpoint")
1999	            robot_ids.add(robot_id)
2000	            task_id = record.get("task_id")
2001	            if task_id is not None and not isinstance(task_id, str):
2002	                raise ValueError(f"robot {robot_id!r} field 'task_id' must be a string or null")
2003	            if "position" not in record:
2004	                raise ValueError(f"robot {robot_id!r} is missing field 'position'")
2005	            route = record.get("route")
2006	            if not isinstance(route, list):
2007	                raise ValueError(f"robot {robot_id!r} field 'route' must be a list")
2008	            if "distance_travelled" not in record:
2009	                raise ValueError(f"robot {robot_id!r} is missing field 'distance_travelled'")
2010	            robot_records.append(record)
2011	
2012	        task_records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
2013	        task_ids: set[str] = set()
2014	        for index, record in enumerate(raw_tasks):
2015	            if not isinstance(record, dict):
2016	                raise ValueError(f"task entry {index} must be an object")
2017	            task_id = record.get("task_id")
2018	            if not isinstance(task_id, str):
2019	                raise ValueError(f"task entry {index} field 'task_id' must be a string")
2020	            if task_id in task_ids:
2021	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate task id {task_id!r} in checkpoint")
2022	            task_ids.add(task_id)
2023	            assigned = record.get("assigned_robot")
2024	            if assigned is not None and not isinstance(assigned, str):
2025	                raise ValueError(
2026	                    f"task {task_id!r} field 'assigned_robot' must be a string or null"
2027	                )
2028	            if not isinstance(record.get("picked_up"), bool):
2029	                raise ValueError(f"task {task_id!r} field 'picked_up' must be a boolean")
2030	            if not isinstance(record.get("completed"), bool):
2031	                raise ValueError(f"task {task_id!r} field 'completed' must be a boolean")
2032	            if "pickup" not in record:
2033	                raise ValueError(f"task {task_id!r} is missing field 'pickup'")
2034	            if "dropoff" not in record:
2035	                raise ValueError(f"task {task_id!r} is missing field 'dropoff'")
2036	            task_records.append(record)
2037	
2038	        positions = [
2039	            tuple(record["position"])
2040	            for record in robot_records
2041	            if isinstance(record["position"], list)
2042	            and len(record["position"]) == 2
2043	            and all(_is_int(value) for value in record["position"])
2044	        ]
2045	        if len(positions) != len(set(positions)):
2046	            raise ValueError("checkpoint robots cannot share a position")
2047	        return robot_records, task_records

2061	    @classmethod
2062	    def _load_map_changes(cls, data: Mapping[str, object]) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
2063	        raw = cls._require_field(data, "map_changes")
2064	        if not isinstance(raw, list):
2065	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'map_changes' must be a list")
2066	        changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
2067	        last_tick = -1
2068	        last_sequence = 0
2069	        for index, frame in enumerate(raw):
2070	            context = f"map change {index}"
2071	            if not isinstance(frame, dict):
2072	                raise ValueError(f"{context} must be an object")
2073	            tick = frame.get("tick")
2074	            sequence = frame.get("sequence")
2075	            if not _is_int(tick) or tick < 0:
2076	                raise ValueError(f"{context} field 'tick' must be a non-negative integer")
2077	            if not _is_int(sequence) or sequence <= 0:
2078	                raise ValueError(f"{context} field 'sequence' must be a positive integer")
2079	            if sequence != index + 1:
2080	                raise ValueError(
2081	                    f"map change sequences must run consecutively from 1; change {index} "
2082	                    f"has sequence {sequence}, expected {index + 1}"
2083	                )
2084	            if tick < last_tick:
2085	                raise ValueError(
2086	                    f"{context} tick {tick} is earlier than a preceding map change"
2087	                )
2088	            if tick == last_tick and sequence != last_sequence + 1:
2089	                raise ValueError(f"{context} breaks consecutive sequencing at tick {tick}")
2090	            added = cls._load_change_cells(frame.get("added"), context, "added")
2091	            removed = cls._load_change_cells(frame.get("removed"), context, "removed")
2092	            if not added and not removed:
2093	                raise ValueError(f"{context} contains no actual obstacle changes")
2094	            overlap = set(added) & set(removed)
2095	            if overlap:
2096	                cell = sorted(overlap)[0]
2097	                raise ValueError(
2098	                    f"{context} adds and removes the same cell {list(cell)}"
2099	                )
2100	            changes.append(
2101	                {
2102	                    "type": "map_change",
2103	                    "tick": tick,
2104	                    "sequence": sequence,
2105	                    "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
2106	                    "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
2107	                }
2108	            )
2109	            last_tick = tick
2110	            last_sequence = sequence
2111	        return changes

2113	    @classmethod
2114	    def _validate_map_history(
2115	        cls,
2116	        base_grid: GridMap,
2117	        saved_grid: GridMap,
2118	        changes: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]],
2119	    ) -> None:
2120	        obstacles = set(base_grid.obstacles)
2121	        width, height = saved_grid.width, saved_grid.height
2122	        for frame in changes:
2123	            for key in ("added", "removed"):
2124	                for cell in frame[key]:
2125	                    x, y = cell
2126	                    if not (0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height):
2127	                        raise ValueError(
2128	                            f"map change {frame['sequence']} cell {list(cell)} lies "
2129	                            "outside the map"
2130	                        )
2131	            added = {tuple(cell) for cell in frame["added"]}
2132	            removed = {tuple(cell) for cell in frame["removed"]}
2133	            for cell in added:
2134	                if cell in obstacles:
2135	                    raise ValueError(
2136	                        f"map change {frame['sequence']} adds obstacle {list(cell)} "
2137	                        "that is already present according to the history"
2138	                    )
2139	            for cell in removed:
2140	                if cell not in obstacles:
2141	                    raise ValueError(
2142	                        f"map change {frame['sequence']} removes obstacle {list(cell)} "
2143	                        "that is absent according to the history"
2144	                    )
2145	            obstacles |= added
2146	            obstacles -= removed
2147	        if obstacles != set(saved_grid.obstacles):
2148	            raise ValueError(
2149	                "the map reproduced from 'map_changes' does not match the saved grid"
2150	            )

2152	    @staticmethod
2153	    def _history_closed_cells(
2154	        base_grid: GridMap,
2155	        changes: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]],
2156	    ) -> frozenset[Position]:
2157	        """Cells open on the base map that the recorded edits net-close.
2158	
2159	        The change history is replayed from *base_grid* (its validity and
2160	        reproduction of the saved grid are checked separately by
2161	        :meth:`_validate_map_history`), and the result holds exactly the cells
2162	        a preset-route robot may legitimately still name while waiting: open
2163	        in the initial map, closed later by an accepted edit, and still closed
2164	        at save time. A cell closed and reopened before the save nets to open
2165	        and is therefore absent, as is every base-map obstacle.
2166	        """
2167	        obstacles = set(base_grid.obstacles)
2168	        for frame in changes:
2169	            obstacles.update(tuple(cell) for cell in frame["added"])
2170	            obstacles.difference_update(tuple(cell) for cell in frame["removed"])
2171	        return frozenset(obstacles - set(base_grid.obstacles))

2173	    @classmethod
2174	    def _replay_map_change_frames(
2175	        cls, replay: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]]
2176	    ) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
2177	        frames = [frame for frame in replay if frame.get("type") == "map_change"]

2302	    @staticmethod
2303	    def _validate_active_task_routes(
2304	        paused: set[str],
2305	        task_by_id: Mapping[str, Task],
2306	        robot_by_id: Mapping[str, Robot],
2307	    ) -> None:
2308	        """Reject routes that cannot finish the task each robot is bound to.
2309	
2310	        Traversability and adjacency are checked elsewhere. This enforces the
2311	        pickup/delivery business rules -- the very same waypoint requirement
2312	        :func:`_task_route_waypoints` plans with -- for tasks that are
2313	        assigned, unfinished and not paused by map unreachability: a non-empty
2314	        route must end at the dropoff, and a robot that has not collected yet
2315	        -- and is not already standing on the pickup cell -- must still pass
2316	        through the pickup. Passing the dropoff early changes nothing; the
2317	        route only has to reach the pickup and return, and saved avoidance
2318	        detours need not match a replanned shortest route. Empty routes are
2319	        legal only when no remaining waypoint is required: the loaded robot is
2320	        already at the dropoff, or position, pickup and dropoff all coincide
2321	        (the goods are collected on resume). Paused tasks keep their empty-route
2322	        exemption, and unassigned or completed tasks are not judged as work in
2323	        progress.
2324	        """
2325	        for task in task_by_id.values():
2326	            if task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
2327	                continue
2328	            if task.task_id in paused:
2329	                # Map-unreachability pauses legitimately carry an empty route
2330	                # regardless of pickup state; the binding itself is all that
2331	                # must survive.
2332	                continue
2333	            robot = robot_by_id.get(task.assigned_robot)
2334	            if robot is None or robot.task_id != task.task_id:
2335	                # Ownership mismatches of this kind are reported separately.
2336	                continue
2337	            route = robot.route
2338	            label = (
2339	                f"task {task.task_id!r} assigned to robot {robot.robot_id!r}"
2340	            )
2341	            required = _task_route_waypoints(robot.position, task)
2342	            if route:
2343	                if route[-1] != task.dropoff:
2344	                    raise ValueError(
2345	                        f"{label} has a remaining route that ends at "
2346	                        f"{list(route[-1])} instead of its dropoff "
2347	                        f"{list(task.dropoff)}"
2348	                    )
2349	                if task.pickup in required and task.pickup not in route:
2350	                    raise ValueError(
2351	                        f"{label} has not picked up the goods and its remaining "
2352	                        f"route never reaches the pickup point "
2353	                        f"{list(task.pickup)} on the way to its dropoff "
2354	                        f"{list(task.dropoff)}"
2355	                    )
2356	            elif task.picked_up:
2357	                if robot.position != task.dropoff:
2358	                    raise ValueError(
2359	                        f"{label} has an empty remaining route with the goods "
2360	                        f"already picked up but the robot is at "
2361	                        f"{list(robot.position)}, not at the dropoff "
2362	                        f"{list(task.dropoff)}"
2363	                    )
2364	            elif required:
2365	                raise ValueError(
2366	                    f"{label} has an empty remaining route before pickup: the "
2367	                    "task can only resume when the robot position, pickup "
2368	                    f"{list(task.pickup)} and dropoff {list(task.dropoff)} all "
2369	                    "coincide"

2372	    @classmethod
2373	    def _iter_replay_events(
2374	        cls, data: Mapping[str, object]
2375	    ) -> Iterator[tuple[int, dict[str, object], object]]:
2376	        """Yield ``(index, frame, frame_type)`` for every replay event in order.
2377	
2378	        This is the single place that owns the ordinary-tick-frame rules both
2379	        format versions share, so they are never maintained twice: the
2380	        ``replay`` field must be a list, every frame must be an object, a
2381	        missing ``type`` means an ordinary tick frame, and tick frames must be
2382	        numbered consecutively from 1 -- map-change events sit between ticks
2383	        without consuming a number -- with a well-formed payload (checked via
2384	        the equally shared :meth:`_validate_tick_frame_payload`). Anything
2385	        beyond that stays with the two loaders: version 1 rejects non-tick
2386	        frames and normalizes the ``type`` field, version 2 keeps its own
2387	        event-type dispatch and map-change ordering checks. The scan is lazy,
2388	        so each frame is examined exactly when the consuming loader reaches it
2389	        and the first problem is reported in the same order as before.
2390	        """
2391	        raw = cls._require_field(data, "replay")
2392	        if not isinstance(raw, list):
2393	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'replay' must be a list")
2394	        tick_index = 0
2395	        for index, frame in enumerate(raw):
2396	            if not isinstance(frame, dict):
2397	                raise ValueError(f"replay frame {index} must be an object")
2398	            frame_type = frame.get("type", "tick")
2399	            if frame_type == "tick":
2400	                tick_index += 1
2401	                frame_tick = frame.get("tick")
2402	                if not _is_int(frame_tick):
2403	                    raise ValueError(f"replay frame {index} field 'tick' must be an integer")
2404	                if frame_tick != tick_index:
2405	                    raise ValueError(
2406	                        "replay tick numbers must run consecutively from 1; frame "
2407	                        f"{index} has tick {frame_tick}, expected {tick_index}"
2408	                    )
2409	                cls._validate_tick_frame_payload(frame, frame_tick)
2410	            yield index, frame, frame_type

2412	    @classmethod
2413	    def _load_replay(cls, data: Mapping[str, object]) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
2414	        replay: list[dict[str, object]] = []
2415	        tick_index = 0
2416	        last_map_tick = -1
2417	        last_map_sequence = 0
2418	        for index, frame, frame_type in cls._iter_replay_events(data):
2419	            if frame_type == "tick":
2420	                tick_index += 1
2421	                replay.append(frame)
2422	            elif frame_type == "map_change":
2423	                tick = frame.get("tick")
2424	                sequence = frame.get("sequence")
2425	                if not _is_int(tick) or tick < 0:
2426	                    raise ValueError(f"replay frame {index} map change tick must be a non-negative integer")
2427	                if not _is_int(sequence) or sequence <= 0:
2428	                    raise ValueError(f"replay frame {index} map change sequence must be positive")
2429	                if tick != tick_index:
2430	                    raise ValueError(
2431	                        f"replay map change {sequence} is stamped tick {tick} but appears "
2432	                        f"after {tick_index} tick frames"
2433	                    )
2434	                if tick < last_map_tick or (
2435	                    tick == last_map_tick and sequence != last_map_sequence + 1
2436	                ):
2437	                    raise ValueError(
2438	                        f"replay map change {sequence} is out of order at tick {tick}"
2439	                    )
2440	                added = cls._load_change_cells(frame.get("added"), f"replay frame {index}", "added")
2441	                removed = cls._load_change_cells(frame.get("removed"), f"replay frame {index}", "removed")
2442	                replay.append(
2443	                    {
2444	                        "type": "map_change",
2445	                        "tick": tick,
2446	                        "sequence": sequence,
2447	                        "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
2448	                        "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
2449	                    }
2450	                )
2451	                last_map_tick = tick
2452	                last_map_sequence = sequence
2453	            else:
2454	                raise ValueError(f"replay frame {index} has unknown type {frame_type!r}")
2455	        return replay

2496	    @classmethod
2497	    def _validate_replay_positions(
2498	        cls,
2499	        replay: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]],
2500	        tick: int,
2501	        robot_by_id: Mapping[str, Robot],
2502	        base_grid: GridMap,
2503	        changes: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]] = (),
2504	    ) -> None:
2505	        """Reject history that the simulator could never have produced.
2506	
2507	        Every tick frame is checked against the map in effect *during* that
2508	        tick: positions must be in bounds and traversable, no two robots may
2509	        share a cell, each robot may only wait or step one orthogonal cell
2510	        between consecutive tick frames, two robots may not swap cells within
2511	        one tick, and ``moved`` must list exactly the robots whose positions
2512	        changed.
2513	
2514	        Version 2 map changes take effect after the tick they are stamped on,
2515	        in their recorded order: the frame for tick *t* is judged against the
2516	        base grid plus every change stamped below *t*, then the changes stamped
2517	        *t* are applied and may not add obstacles onto cells frame *t* shows a
2518	        robot on -- even when a later change of the same tick removes the cell
2519	        again. Tick-0 changes precede the first frame. Adjacency is always
2520	        judged between neighboring tick frames; a map change between them never
2521	        moves a robot.
2522	
2523	        Version 1 files pass no changes, so the saved grid governs every frame.
2524	        The first frame has no recorded predecessor: its cells, overlaps and
2525	        ``moved`` ids are still checked, but neither the distance of the first
2526	        moves nor the first ``moved`` list is second-guessed.
2527	        """
2528	        tick_frames = [frame for frame in replay if frame.get("type") == "tick"]
2529	        if len(tick_frames) != tick:
2530	            raise ValueError(
2531	                f"replay has {len(tick_frames)} tick frames but the checkpoint is at tick {tick}"
2532	            )
2533	
2534	        expected_ids = set(robot_by_id)
2535	
2536	        def frame_positions(frame: Mapping[str, object]) -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]]:
2537	            raw = frame["robots"]
2538	            assert isinstance(raw, dict)
2539	            if set(raw) != expected_ids:
2540	                raise ValueError(
2541	                    f"replay frame {frame['tick']} robot ids do not match current robots"
2542	                )
2543	            return {robot_id: tuple(position) for robot_id, position in raw.items()}
2544	
2545	        # A non-zero-tick history must end exactly where the saved robots stand
2546	        # before any deeper history check runs.
2547	        if tick > 0:
2548	            last_positions = frame_positions(tick_frames[-1])

2552	                        "last replay frame positions do not match current robot positions "
2553	                        f"for robot {robot_id!r}"

2565	            because the unrecorded initial layout cannot be reconstructed.

2570	                sequence = change["sequence"]
2571	                added = {tuple(cell) for cell in change["added"]}
2572	                for cell in added:

2576	                            "the initial layout before tick 1"

2579	                        )

2582	                            f"{list(cell)} occupied by robot {robot_id!r} in {when}"

2586	                    {tuple(cell) for cell in change["removed"]}

2588	                change_index += 1

2591	        # checkpoint is still at tick 0 the saved robot positions *are* the
2592	        # layout of that moment; otherwise they cannot be reconstructed.
2593	        initial_occupants = (
2594	            {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in robot_by_id.values()}
2595	            if tick == 0
2596	            else {}
2597	        )
2598	        apply_changes(0, initial_occupants)
2599	
2600	        previous: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] | None = None
2601	        for frame in tick_frames:
2602	            frame_tick = frame["tick"]
2603	            # The grid here still reflects only changes stamped below this
2604	            # tick -- exactly the map the robots moved on during this tick.
2605	            positions = frame_positions(frame)

2612	                        f"{list(position)}, outside the map in effect at tick {frame_tick}"
2613	                    )

2616	                        f"replay frame {frame_tick} robot {robot_id!r} is at "
2617	                        f"{list(position)}, an obstacle on the map in effect at tick "
2618	                        f"{frame_tick}"
2619	                    )

2624	                if occupant is not None:

2626	                        f"replay frame {frame_tick} robots {occupant!r} and {robot_id!r} "
2627	                        f"both occupy cell {list(position)}"

2634	            for robot_id in moved:

2637	                        f"replay frame {frame_tick} 'moved' lists unknown robot "

2639	                    )

2652	                    if distance > 1:
2653	                        raise ValueError(
2654	                            f"replay frame {frame_tick} robot {robot_id!r} moves more "
2655	                            f"than one cell, from {list(old)} to {list(position)}"
2656	                        )
2657	                    if distance == 1:
2658	                        actually_moved.add(robot_id)
2659	                mover_ids = sorted(actually_moved)
2660	                for index, robot_id in enumerate(mover_ids):
2661	                    for other_id in mover_ids[index + 1 :]:
2662	                        if (
2663	                            positions[robot_id] == previous[other_id]
2664	                            and positions[other_id] == previous[robot_id]
2665	                        ):
2666	                            raise ValueError(
2667	                                f"replay frame {frame_tick} robots {robot_id!r} and "
2668	                                f"{other_id!r} swap cells "
2669	                                f"{list(previous[robot_id])} and {list(positions[robot_id])} "
2670	                                "within one tick"
